full_judgment: 2. The case of the petitioners is that a Hat named Baluchar Hat was running within Mouza Baluchar, PS Shirajdikhan, District Munshiganj. The land of the said Hat was submerged in the process of erosion and was engulfed by Dhaleswari river in 1396 BS. The Hat-going people with theactive support of the then Upazila Administration started a Bazar in the nearby land belonging to the petitioners without their consent. However, the said Hat was running well in the name of Baluchar Munshir Hat. Nter expiry of 1396 BS the owners of the land approaced the Government for setting up of the Bazar under the East-Pakistan Hat and Bazar (Establishment and Acquisition) Ordinance, 1959 as amended. Thereafter, the Government issued licence to the owners of the land including the petitioners permitting them to continue with the Bazar vide Memo No.5/4/Rajasha/l1.6.89 dated 4.4.90 issued by the Deputy Commissioner, Munshiganj for the year 1397 BS. Thereafter, the licence was renewed for 1398 BS. Thereafter, for renewal of licence for the year 1399 BS a sum or Taka 44,250.00 was demanded and it was mentioned in the demand note that it was for a temporary period and that the licensees would be bound by any future allotment for the Hat Bazar as may be made by the Government. The licensees did not deposit the renewal fee and made representation to the Government for waiving the condition attached to the renewal order (Annexure-D) and requested the authority concerned to renew the licence in the name of Baluchar Munshir Hat Bazar as before. Thereafter, the District Administration directed the licensees to deposit the renewal fee for a period of 5 months from Baisak to Bhadra, 1399 BS with intimation that proposal for naming the Hat after individual name has been rejected. Against the said order, the petitioners preferred an appeal before the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka Division under section 147 of the East Bengal Estate Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The said appeal was registered as Appeal No. 103 of 1992 and it was admitted and the records were called for and during pendency of the appeal the operation of the impugned order was stayed. The petitioners were informed by some of the shopkeepers that they were asked to remove their shops with structures to a nearby land wherein a Hat has been established in the name of Baluchar Hat. The petitioners after enquiry came to know that the Ministry of Land vacated the order of stay granted by the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka Division by the impugned order and the Thana Administration has received instructions to demolish the Baluchar Munshir Hat and letters were issued to the shop keepers. The petitioners also came to learn that on an application filed by one Bani Amin, President of Bahichar Hat Bazar Development Committee, the Ministry of Land passed the order directing the Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka to send the case record of the said appeal to that Ministry if it could not be disposed of within 11.11.93 No notice was issued to the petitioners when the records were called for nor when the order of stay was vacated.
